links.outcome: Run-to-run variability and input format effects on LLM coding agreement
links.effect: Each prompt tested 3 times to account for run-to-run variability (kappa ranges reported); plain-text pasting gave kappa ≈0.6-0.7 vs 0.2-0.4 for spreadsheet upload.
links.quote: To account for run-to-run variability, each prompt strategy was tested 3 times on the same 20% subsample ( n = 70 for Category 1; n = 40 for Category 2), with mean percent agreement and Cohen’s κ reported ( Tables 2 and 3 ).

links.effect: Plain-text input had κ ≈ 0.6-0.7 versus spreadsheet upload κ ≈ 0.2-0.4.
links.quote: Next, interface effects emerged as critical: performance was notably higher when comments were pasted as plain text directly into the chat compared with when they were uploaded as spreadsheets, where the model often defaulted to keyword matching (κ ≈ 0.6-0.7 vs 0.2-0.4; see Table S7 ).

links.effect: Spreadsheet uploads lowered performance to κ ≈ 0.2-0.4 compared with plain text κ ≈ 0.6-0.7.
links.quote: Next, interface effects emerged as critical: performance was notably higher when comments were pasted as plain text directly into the chat compared with when they were uploaded as spreadsheets, where the model often defaulted to keyword matching (κ ≈ 0.6-0.7 vs 0.2-0.4; see Table S7 ).

links.effect: Category 2 baseline performance was 48%, κ = 0.42; final calibrated performance was 83%, κ = 0.78.
links.quote: In contrast, Category 2 showed much weaker baseline performance (48%, κ = 0.42, moderate).

links.effect: Role + context raised Category 2 agreement to 73% (κ = 0.73); all strategies reached 83% (κ = 0.76) in Category 1.
links.quote: Here, prompt refinements made a much larger difference: role + context (I1) yielded the greatest improvement, raising agreement to 73% (κ = 0.73, substantial).
